## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible math walk (walk1) can be compiled to vectorized code approaching the streaming ceiling, even though the RNG-order-dependent walk2 must remain scalar.

## Cache saturation
The smallest measured N=4000 already exceeds the L1d spill point (N≈963), so the L1d→L2 transition is not directly observed. From N=4000 to N=65000 (the L2 spill at N≈61680), cost FALLS from 40.063 to 28.911 ns/p at q=0.01 — overhead amortization dominates small N. At the L2→DRAM spill there is no knee: cost stays FLAT at ~30–31 ns/p from N=65000 through N=4000000. Death rate raises the floor modestly (q=0.25 averages ~32 ns/p vs ~30 ns/p at q=0.01) without changing the N-shape, indicating the respawn/scatter path adds per-particle overhead but does not alter the memory-access pattern.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.35 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 9.3% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth is essentially flat across all N and death rates (2.08–2.35 GB/s), never approaching the ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound: the low and invariant achieved bandwidth indicates that per-particle compute and scatter logic, not memory transfer, sets the cost. There is no transition to a bandwidth-bound regime at any N or death rate.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: the histogram shows 0 vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar — `fmul s5`, `fadd s5`, `fsub s5`, `fcvtzs` — operating on individual particle components loaded via `ldp s5, s6` (scalar pairs). The math walk is delegated to `_halide_b2_math` (a `bl` call), but the surrounding particle loop is entirely scalar. The scatter into the image buffer uses byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` pairs with `csel`-based clamping to `#0xff` for each of three RGB channels (`strb w2, [x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x2]`), repeated across four neighbor offsets. No gather instructions appear. The scalar codegen and byte-granular scatter explain why achieved bandwidth stays at 9% of ceiling: the processor issues scalar loads and byte stores that cannot saturate the memory subsystem.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 2.35 GB/s (9.3% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate, and the step function contains zero vector instructions. The `bl _halide_b2_math` call does not rescue the scalar particle loop, whose byte-granular `strb` scatter and scalar `fmul`/`fcvtzs`/`csel` clamp logic dominate cost. The hypothesis that Halide-expressible math could approach the streaming ceiling fails because the non-vectorizable walk2 and scatter path caps performance far below it.
